title: MG90S Metal Gear Servos are NON-NEGOTIABLE — SG90 Plastic Fails in Every Build
context: Pan-tilt mechanism for water gun aiming. Servos must handle unbalanced load of water-filled pistol + dynamic slosh forces.
what_was_found: EVERY documented water gun turret project (ESP32-CAM, Raspberry Pi, Arduino) reports that plastic SG90 servo gears strip within hours of operation when carrying an electric water pistol. The dave-ct/ai_object_plus_water project specifically abandoned the Pimoroni pan-tilt HAT because 'the servos did not have the power to support the water pistol components.' The ESP32-CAM water gun project explicitly recommends MG90S over SG90. The Cat Deterrent Turret project went further, using NEMA17 stepper motors for higher torque.

specifications.sg90: Plastic gears, 1.2 kg·cm stall torque, ~9g — FAILS under water pistol load
specifications.mg90s: Metal gears, 1.8-2.2 kg·cm stall torque, ~13g — MINIMUM for water pistol
specifications.mg996r: Metal gears, 10 kg·cm stall torque, ~55g — overkill for weight budget, used in TrackingPanTiltCam
specifications.nema17: Stepper, highest torque, ~280g — too heavy for Splash

source: Hour 7 Competitor Analysis — Multiple projects across ESP32-CAM, Raspberry Pi, Arduino ecosystems
action: Update Splash BOM: replace SG90 with MG90S (2× ~13g = 26g total, +8g over SG90). Acceptable weight penalty for guaranteed reliability.
